# Tye — Qualia (SEP, 2024)

## Chicago 18 forms

**Full note:** Michael Tye, “Qualia,” *The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy*, Spring 2024 Edition, ed. Edward N. Zalta and Uri Nodelman (Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University, 2024), §1, https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/spr2024/entries/qualia/.

**Shortened note:** Tye, “Qualia,” §1.

**Bibliography:** Tye, Michael. “Qualia.” *The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy*. Spring 2024 Edition. Edited by Edward N. Zalta and Uri Nodelman. Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University, 2024. https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/spr2024/entries/qualia/.

## Essay use

Tye fixes the phenomenal-character boundary that objective internality must not cross. It keeps an operational context-world separate from a claim about what it is like for a subject to undergo experience.

**Claim boundary:** the entry does not establish that artificial agents have or lack qualia, and it does not settle consciousness metaphysics.

- **Status:** quotation-ready.

## Passage card — `tye-2024-qualia-sep-q002` — dispute remains live
